name: vscwclang
description: Build, run and debug C and C++ with Clang in VS Code for the Web, entirely in your browser. Nothing to install.

C_Cpp.default.defines.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as a fallback for `vscwclang.flags` (as `-D`) when that is unset; see `vscwclang.useCppToolsSettings`.

C_Cpp.default.includePath.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as a fallback for `vscwclang.flags` (as `-I`) when that is unset.

C_Cpp.default.compilerArgs.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as a fallback for `vscwclang.flags` when that is unset.

C_Cpp.default.cppStandard.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as `-std=` for C++ files when `vscwclang.flags` is unset (for example `c++20`).

C_Cpp.default.cStandard.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as `-std=` for C files when `vscwclang.flags` is unset (for example `c17`).

C_Cpp.default.compileCommands.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as `vscwclang.compileCommands` when that is empty.

C_Cpp.default.forcedInclude.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Workspace files added to every compile as `-include <file>`; also read from `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json`, which wins when both set it. Needs `vscwclang.useCppToolsSettings` and is replaced by an explicit `vscwclang.flags`.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.parameterNames.enabled.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Sets clangd's `InlayHints: ParameterNames`. cpptools defaults this to off and clangd to on, so nothing changes until it is set. Reload the window to apply; `editor.inlayHints.enabled` still decides whether hints are shown.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.autoDeclarationTypes.en.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Sets clangd's `InlayHints: DeducedTypes` (the types of `auto` declarations). cpptools defaults this to off and clangd to on, so nothing changes until it is set. Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.autoDeclarationTypes.sh.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd has no option for it); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.parameterNames.hideLead.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd has no option for it); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.parameterNames.suppress.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd has no option for it); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.referenceOperator.enabl.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd has no option for it); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.inlayHints.referenceOperator.showS.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd has no option for it); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.files.exclude.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Merged into `vscwclang.files.exclude` unless `vscwclang.useCppToolsSettings` is off.

C_Cpp.formatting.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. `disabled` turns off Format Document, Format Selection and format-on-type; every other value uses the clang-format built into clangd (`vcFormat` is not available). Needs `vscwclang.intelliSense.enabled`, because clangd does the formatting. Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.clang_format_style.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible, but only `file` is supported: clangd uses the nearest `.clang-format` file. Another value is logged; put `BasedOnStyle: <name>` in a `.clang-format` file instead.

C_Cpp.clang_format_fallbackStyle.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. The style used when there is no `.clang-format` file, passed as clangd's `-fallback-style=`: `LLVM`, `Google`, `Chromium`, `Mozilla`, `WebKit`, `Microsoft`, `GNU` or `none`. `Visual Studio` means `Microsoft`. Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.clang_format_sortIncludes.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible, but not supported: set `SortIncludes` in a `.clang-format` file instead. A value is logged.

C_Cpp.clang_format_path.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible, but ignored: the clang-format built into clangd is always used.

C_Cpp.refactoring.includeHeader.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. `never` becomes clangd's `-header-insertion=never`; `always` and `ifNeeded` use clangd's default (insert the `#include` of an accepted completion when it is missing). Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.enabled.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. `false` starts clangd with `-clang-tidy=false`. Otherwise clangd runs clang-tidy with the checks in the workspace's `.clang-tidy` plus `checks.enabled`. Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.checks.enab.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Check globs (such as `bugprone-*`) added to clangd's clang-tidy checks. Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.checks.disa.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Check globs removed from clangd's clang-tidy checks. Reload the window to apply.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.headerFilte.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd reads clang-tidy options only from `.clang-tidy` files); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.config.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd reads clang-tidy options only from `.clang-tidy` files); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.fallbackCon.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd reads clang-tidy options only from `.clang-tidy` files); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args.markdownDescription: Not supported (clangd reads clang-tidy options only from `.clang-tidy` files); a note is logged when it is set.

C_Cpp.loggingLevel.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. Read as `vscwclang.loggingLevel` when that is unset.

C_Cpp.intelliSenseEngine.markdownDescription: cpptools-compatible. `disabled` turns clangd off when `vscwclang.intelliSense.enabled` is unset.

vscwclang.toolchainUrl.markdownDescription: Development override: directory URL serving a toolchain made by `scripts/make-toolchain-dist.mjs` (`manifest.json` plus chunks). When set, the manifest is trusted as served instead of being checked against the hash pinned in the extension. Leave empty to use the pinned toolchain. The host must send CORS and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` headers.

vscwclang.flags.markdownDescription: Extra flags for `vscwClang: Build` and `Build and Run`. `/workspace` is your workspace folder, so the default `-I/workspace` lets sources include headers relative to the project root (`#include "utils/foo.hpp"`). `-l`, `-L` and `-Wl,` flags go to the linker; restricted flags (`--target`, `-o`, ...) are rejected. A task's own `flags` replace these. When you have not set this, flags from cpptools' `C_Cpp.default.defines`, `includePath` (workspace paths only), `cppStandard` and `cStandard` (each applied only to its own language), and `compilerArgs` are added too (see `vscwclang.useCppToolsSettings`).  `${workspaceFolder}` (as `/workspace`), `${workspaceFolderBasename}`, `${file}` and the other file variables are expanded; `${env:}`, `${command:}` and `${input:}` are not supported.

vscwclang.sourceGlobs.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, of the source files that `vscwClang: Build` compiles together into one program. Narrow this (e.g. `["src/**/*.cpp"]`) when the folder holds several programs, such as tests that each define `main`. A leading `${workspaceFolder}/` is accepted and ignored.

vscwclang.compileCommands.markdownDescription: Workspace-relative path of the `compile_commands.json` that Build and Run use when there is no default `tasks.json` build task; a string or a list, of which the first is used (same shape as cpptools' `C_Cpp.default.compileCommands`, which is the fallback when this is empty; `${workspaceFolder}/` prefixes are accepted). Empty looks for `compile_commands.json`, then `build/compile_commands.json`. Each source is compiled with the flags of its own entry; a CMake database with several targets asks which one to build.

vscwclang.compileCommandsInclude.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, that narrow which `compile_commands.json` entries are linked into the program (for databases of several programs that do not name CMake targets). Empty keeps them all. A leading `${workspaceFolder}/` is accepted and ignored.

vscwclang.files.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, of files and folders that are never compiled or indexed: IDE scratch folders and build output by default. Same shape as cpptools' `C_Cpp.files.exclude` (`true` excludes, `false` un-excludes a default), which is merged in unless `vscwclang.useCppToolsSettings` is off. Supports `**`, `*`, `?` and `{a,b}`, ignoring case. A file named explicitly by a task or compile database is never excluded. A leading `${workspaceFolder}/` is accepted and ignored.

vscwclang.run.args.markdownDescription: Arguments for `vscwClang: Build and Run`. A `launch.json` configuration (`cppdbg`, `cppvsdbg`, `lldb`, `codelldb`) that has `args` takes precedence. `vscwClang: Build and Run with Arguments...` asks each time instead (pre-filled with the last answer).  `${workspaceFolder}` (as `/workspace`), `${workspaceFolderBasename}`, `${file}` and the other file variables are expanded; `${env:}`, `${command:}` and `${input:}` are not supported.

enumDescriptions: Run programs on the extension's own WebAssembly host (the default; also used by Debug).

Run programs in a Wasmer (WASIX) sandbox. Needs `vscwclang.wasmerSdkUrl`. The workspace is copied into the sandbox when the program starts and changed files are copied back when it ends; `/tmp` is the sandbox's own and there is no persistent `/home/user`. Experimental.
vscwclang.run.host.markdownDescription: Which host runs Build and Run's program. Debug always uses the extension's own host.

vscwclang.wasmerSdkUrl.markdownDescription: URL of a folder serving `@wasmer/sdk` (its `dist/` and `pkg/` folders), used when `vscwclang.run.host` is `wasmer`. The host must send CORS and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` headers. Experimental.

vscwclang.run.env.markdownDescription: Environment variables for the program, added to the defaults `HOME=/home/user`, `TMPDIR=/tmp`, `USER=user`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`. Set a variable to `null` to remove a default. `${workspaceFolder}` and the other variables are expanded in values (as in `vscwclang.run.args`).

vscwclang.buildCache.maxAgeDays.markdownDescription: Compiled objects kept for faster rebuilds are deleted when no build has used them for this many days. Takes effect at the next build.

vscwclang.buildCache.maxSizeMB.markdownDescription: Most megabytes of compiled objects to keep; the least recently used are deleted first. `vscwClang: Clear build cache` removes them all.

vscwclang.threads.markdownDescription: Build programs for the threaded standard library (`wasm32-wasip1-threads`), so `std::thread`, `std::mutex`, `std::async` and `pthread` work. Programs use shared memory and a larger reserved address space. `-pthread` or `-lpthread` in your flags selects it even when this is off. Turn off for a plain single-threaded build. Needs a window reload for IntelliSense.

vscwclang.precompiledHeaders.markdownDescription: Compile C++ sources against a prebuilt copy of the common standard headers (`<vector>`, `<string>`, `<iostream>`, ...), which cuts the time of each recompiled file by half or more. Used only when your flags match one that was prebuilt (`-std=c++17`, `c++20` or the `gnu++` forms of them, with no `-O` or `-O2`, and no `-D` of a reserved name or `NDEBUG`). Side effect: these headers count as included at the top of every such file, so a missing `#include` goes unnoticed here and fails elsewhere. Turn off to compile exactly as written.

vscwclang.parallelCompiles.markdownDescription: How many source files to compile at once, each in its own Worker. `0` picks automatically (the browser's core count minus one, at most 4). Each compile can use several hundred MB, so lower this if the tab runs out of memory.

vscwclang.toolTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Seconds to wait for each clang or wasm-ld invocation before stopping it and reporting an error. Compilers print nothing while working, so a crashed run cannot be told apart from a slow one; raise this for very large sources. `0` disables the timeout.

vscwclang.useCppToolsSettings.markdownDescription: Use the C/C++ extension's `C_Cpp.default.*` settings (`defines`, `includePath`, `cppStandard`, `cStandard`, `compilerArgs`) as extra flags when `vscwclang.flags` is not set, and its `C_Cpp.files.exclude`, `C_Cpp.default.compileCommands`, `C_Cpp.loggingLevel` and `C_Cpp.intelliSenseEngine` as defaults. Lets a project configured for cpptools on desktop work here unchanged.

vscwclang.intelliSense.enabled.markdownDescription: Run the clangd language server for completion, hover, go-to-definition and as-you-type diagnostics. Turn off to skip clangd's download, memory use and indexing when you only need Build and Run. Defaults to off if `C_Cpp.intelliSenseEngine` is `disabled`. Reload the window to apply.

vscwclang.loggingLevel.markdownDescription: How much of clangd's log to show in the `vscwclang` output channel (same values as cpptools' `C_Cpp.loggingLevel`, which is the default when this is unset). `None` and `Error` show only errors. Reload the window to apply.

commands.title: vscwClang: Build and Run C++ with Arguments... (clang.wasm)

program.description: Not used yet: Debug builds the workspace in debug mode (the same sources and flags as Run) and debugs the result.

console.description: Where the program's input and output go: a terminal you can type into (default), or the Debug Console (output only; a program that reads input then waits forever).

stopOnEntry.description: Stop at the first instrumented block of the program instead of running to the first breakpoint.

command.description: g++, gcc, clang++ or clang (a full path is fine). The arguments are mapped onto a browser build; see the vscwClang README.

sources.description: Source globs relative to the workspace folder. Default: all .c/.cc/.cpp/.cxx files.

flags.description: Extra clang flags; -l, -L and -Wl, flags go to wasm-ld.

output.description: Output .wasm, relative to the workspace folder.

scripts.pretest: node scripts/make-toolchain-dist.mjs --release llvm-artifacts --mtdist llvm-artifacts/mtdist --if-missing && npm run compile-web
scripts.compile-web: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package-web: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
